full.description: This image is a blood smear micrograph showing erythrocytes and a neutrophil. Within the neutrophil, two distinct yeast forms are visible, characterized by their round to oval shape with surrounding halos. These findings are indicative of candidemia, showing yeast forms phagocytized by a neutrophil in the peripheral blood.

blind.description: This image is a blood smear micrograph stained with Wright's stain. It shows peripheral blood components, including a neutrophil and red blood cells. Ring-form trophozoites are visible within the erythrocytes. The findings are most consistent with an infection of Plasmodium vivax causing malaria.

random.description: This is a blood smear micrograph showing a stained peripheral blood or bone marrow sample. Red blood cells and nucleated white blood cells are visible, with prominent fungal yeast forms ingested within macrophages or monocytes. The morphology is characteristic of intracellular fungal organisms such as Histoplasma capsulatum. This finding is indicative of disseminated fungal infection.
